Held by no case: the progress line, the line that bash 5 once printed when the progress timer was stopped, that every shard tests one revision (the parent passes one), and a second signal while the parent cleans up (it, and KILL, can leave shards running, their worktrees and the logs directory). The case count of a full run is not pinned and no file in the repository states it: a shorter walk, or a deleted call of `expect_unchanged`, prints a smaller count and passes, and only a person who compares the printed count with the earlier one would see it. The two checks that a refused run left a file alone are counted cases, so the lists and totals cover them and a shard that skips one is refused; deleting one of them lowers the count by one and passes, as deleting any case does, and the script before the sharding was the same.
